section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the superiority of the service of "Basi" over that of "Achosi" and "Imi" is also reflected in the worker's own perception, where in the latter the loftiness of the work is felt, while in "Basi" the worker's self-nullification is felt, making him a vessel for the light drawn down by the mitzvos.
section.t: And one may add,
that the superiority of the service of "Basi" over the service of "Achosi" and "Imi" is also with regard to the person who serves.
For in the service of "Achosi" and "Imi," the fineness of the existence of the serving person is felt,
[namely] the greatness of the elevation of his service
[the elevation of the service itself
(the service of engaging in Torah,
and certainly the service of mesiras nefesh),
and the elevation brought about through his service,
that he becomes a brother to the Holy One, blessed be He, and beyond this, that he, as it were, influences the Holy One, blessed be He],
while in the service of "Basi"
(the fulfillment of the mitzvos)
his self-nullification is felt,
both with regard to the service itself,
that all his service is only to fulfill the command of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and with regard to the drawing down that comes through his service,

that this [drawing down] of the Essence of the Ein Sof through the fulfillment of mitzvos is not due to the aspect of the person who fulfills the mitzvos, but because the mitzvos are the will and command of the Essence.
And it may be said,
that through this self-nullification he becomes a vessel for the light that is drawn down through the mitzvos.
And this is [the meaning of] "For behold, I am coming and I will dwell within you,"
that the drawing down of "I am coming,"
I Myself, as it were,
is "within you,"
in the innermost aspect.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the superiority of the self-nullification of "Basi" over that of "Imi" (mesiras nefesh), explaining that the nullification of accepting the yoke of Heaven still involves the person's own existence, whereas true nullification comes from the Master's side.
section.t: D)
And it must be understood,
that since "Imi" is the service of mesiras nefesh,
and mesiras nefesh is the matter of self-nullification,
and particularly according to what was brought above
(section 2)
that the crown with which the Knesses Yisrael crowned
(His mother)
the Holy One, blessed be He, is through their having preceded "naaseh" to "nishma,"
that the self-nullification of preceding "naaseh" to "nishma" is the self-nullification to the Master of the will,
what is the superiority of the self-nullification of "Basi" over the self-nullification of "Imi"?
And it may be said regarding this,
that the self-nullification of preceding "naaseh" to "nishma"
is that Israel accepted upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven.
Therefore,
even though the self-nullification of accepting the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven is
(not only with regard to his power of action,
that he will do all that he is commanded,
but also)
in his very existence,
that his entire existence is that he is a servant of the King,
the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
nevertheless,
since the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven comes from the person's side,
that he accepted upon himself to be a servant of the King,
behold, in this self-nullification the person's own existence is also mixed in
[and likewise with regard to the mesiras nefesh of the aspect of "Imi,"
that mesiras nefesh is from the nature of the soul].
And the true self-nullification is when the self-nullification is from the Master's side.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the true status of Israel as servants of God is not merely from their own acceptance of the yoke, but because God took them out of Egypt, compelling their servitude, a matter primarily drawn down at the giving of the Torah.
section.t: And it may be said,
that this is what is written,
"For the children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt,"
that this [fact] that Israel are servants of the Holy One, blessed be He, is
(not only because they accepted the yoke of His kingship, may He be blessed,
but also)
because the Holy One, blessed be He, took them out of the land of Egypt,
through which they are compelled to be servants.
And this matter is primarily drawn down at the time of the giving of the Torah.
